correctness.rationale: From Jeřábek's quantifier elimination for the model completion EC_{one unary f}, a complete n-type is exactly a coherent congruence diagram among the iterates f^m(x_i). A finite functional-graph component necessarily becomes periodic; every infinite component has one eventually merged forward ray. For X_k={p:rho(p)>=k}, finite equality data isolating complete periodic components and the finite mergers of distinct rays show a type with exactly k infinite components is relatively isolated in X_k. Conversely every type with rho>k has arbitrarily late ray closure into a directed cycle that preserves any specified finite diagram, produces a distinct type and decreases rho by exactly one. Thus X_k'=X_{k+1} through k=n, the top-rank n type is the unique complete diagram with all f^a(x_i) distinct, and the next derivative is empty. Combined with Jeřábek's countability of S_n, Stone compact metrizability and classical finite-height scattered compacta classification, this gives S_n approximately omega^n+1. The bundled bounded term-diagram checks only test the local mechanism and do not establish the infinite claim.
